_comment: Inputs for /january-paycheck-change-calculator/ that live nowhere else. The 2027 federal figures are NOT here: they come from projections-2027.json (official2027 once the IRS Revenue Procedure is in, the publishers' thirdPartyProjections until then) or from tax-data-2027.json once that file exists, which also replaces every state below. The 2027 Social Security wage base comes from projections-2027.json ssaFactSheet2027.

stateOverrides2027._rule: Only a 2027 figure already set in statute AND already recorded in this repo goes here, patched over the state's 2026 `tax` block for the January paycheck. Everything else uses the 2026 tables, and the page says so. North Carolina added 2026-11-03: S.B. 257 (the 2026 Appropriations Act) is Session Law 2026-41 (ncleg summary title 'S257 - 2026 Appropriations Act. (SL 2026-41)'), already cited in state-payroll-2026.json. Indiana, Mississippi, Nebraska, Montana and New York added 2026-11-03 after a research pass plus an independent refute pass (all 5 CONFIRMED). Nebraska keeps 2026 thresholds and standard deduction (2027 indexed values only in a draft 1040N-ES); Montana, Colorado, North Dakota and Iowa start from federal taxable income, so their 2027 deduction is the federal amount in Rev. Proc. 2026-35 section 3.15 (added 2026-11-06). employeePrograms, where present, replaces the whole list with the state's published 2027 payroll program figures (Washington and New York, added 2026-11-06).

virginia.label: Virginia's 2027 standard deduction
virginia.what: Virginia's standard deduction goes up in 2027, to $9,200 for a single filer and $18,400 for a married couple, under state law. Its $930 personal exemption does not change.
virginia._math: The engine's Virginia standardDeduction field carries the standard deduction plus the personal exemption (see the virginia _source in tax-data-2026.json, 'PERSONAL EXEMPTION FOLDED IN 2026-10-03'): 9,200 + 930 = 10,130 single and head of household; 18,400 + 2 x 930 = 20,260 married filing jointly.
virginia._quote: Va. Code 58.1-322.03(1)(b), currency 8/1/2026: '(vi) for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2027, but before January 1, 2028, $9,200 for single individuals and $18,400 for married persons'. Recorded in tax-data-2026.json virginia _watch and _source.

north-carolina.label: North Carolina's 2027 income tax rate
north-carolina.what: North Carolina's flat income tax rate drops from 3.99% to 3.49% in 2027 under state law, so a little less state tax comes out of each check.
north-carolina._quote: S.L. 2026-41 (S.B. 257, 2026 Appropriations Act, signed 2026-07-07): 3.49% for taxable years 2027-2029, triggers repealed (EY Tax News 2026-1630; ncleg summary S257-SMSA-88(sl)). NCDOR: 3.99% for taxable years after 2025.

indiana.label: Indiana's 2027 income tax rate
indiana.what: Indiana's flat state income tax rate drops from 2.95% to 2.9% in 2027 under state law, so slightly less state tax comes out of each check.
indiana._quote: Indiana DOR, Rates, Fees & Penalties: 'The Indiana Individual adjusted gross income tax rate for 2026 is 2.95% and will adjust in 2027 to 2.90%.' LSA/SBA 2024 Tax Expenditure Review, Table 1: '2026 2.95% / 2027 and after 2.90% / SOURCE: IC 6-3-2-1'. State Budget Agency, Dec 17 2024 forecast presentation: '2.95% in CY 2026 / 2.90% in CY 2027'.
indiana.sourceTitle: Indiana Department of Revenue: Rates, Fees & Penalties

mississippi.label: Mississippi's 2027 income tax rate
mississippi.what: Mississippi's tax on income over $10,000 drops from 4% to 3.75% in 2027 under state law, so a little less state tax comes out of each check.
mississippi._quote: H.B. 1 (2025 Reg. Sess., As Sent to Governor; billstatus history: Approved by Governor), amending Miss. Code 27-7-5(1): '4. For calendar year 2027, on such taxable income, the rate shall be three and three-quarters percent (3.75%)'. MS DOR General Information: 'Tax Year 2027 Excess of $10,000 of Taxable Income is taxed @ 3.75%'.
mississippi.sourceTitle: Mississippi H.B. 1 (2025), Build Up Mississippi Act

nebraska.label: Nebraska's 2027 income tax rate
nebraska.what: Nebraska's top income tax rate drops from 4.55% to 3.99% in 2027 under state law, so a little less state tax comes out of each check for most earners.
nebraska._quote: Governor Pillen release: 'The 2026 income tax rate will fall from 5.2% to 4.55%, with the final stage of the income tax reduction taking effect in 2027, when the rate drops again to 3.99%.' NE DOR 2027 Form 1040N-ES (DRAFT 9/25/2026): 'The tax year 2027 individual income tax rates for the third and fourth brackets are at the same rate of 3.99% per Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2715.03(2)(c)(v).' Thresholds kept at 2026 indexed values; the draft's 2027 indexed thresholds (single 4,270/25,570/41,200; MFJ 8,520/51,150/82,410; HoH 7,960/40,910/61,100) and standard deduction (9,100/18,200/13,400) wait for the final form.
nebraska.sourceTitle: Office of Governor Jim Pillen: income tax cuts effective in January

montana.label: Montana's 2027 income tax brackets
montana.what: In 2027 Montana's 4.7% rate covers more of your income (up to $65,000 single, $130,000 married) and the top rate drops from 5.65% to 5.4%, under state law. Montana starts from federal taxable income, so the 2027 federal standard deduction carries through too.
montana._quote: HB 337 (2025, Ch. 227) section 2 amending MCA 15-30-2103: '(c) ... on the first $20,500 $65,000 of Montana taxable income ... 4.7%; (ii) ... in excess of $20,500 $65,000 ... 5.9%, 5.4%' (MFJ $130,000; HoH $97,500); section 4: the modified inflation factor 'does not apply until tax year 2028'; section 5(3): '[Section 2] is effective January 1, 2027.' MT DOR HB 337 notice, 2027 table: Single '$0.00 to $65,000' 4.7%, 'over $65,000' 5.4%; MFJ $130,000; HoH $97,500.
montana.sourceTitle: Montana Department of Revenue: HB 337 income tax changes

new-york.label: New York's 2027 income tax rates
new-york.what: New York cuts its five lowest income tax rates by another 0.1 point in 2027 under state law, so most middle-income workers see slightly less state tax per check. Paid Family Leave also changes in 2027: 0.452% of pay, up to $451.81 for the year.
new-york._quote: N.Y. Tax Law 601(c)(1)(viii) 'For taxable years beginning after two thousand twenty-six and before two thousand thirty-three': 'Not over $8,500 3.80% ... Over $13,900 but not over $80,650 $572 plus 5.30% ... Over $80,650 but not over $215,400 $4,110 plus 5.80%' (601(a) and (b) item (viii) the same for joint and head of household). NYS Tax Expenditure Report FY2027: 'Beginning with the 2026 tax year, an additional 0.2 percentage point rate reduction will be phased in over two years for all taxpayers with taxable income up to $215,400 ($323,200 for joint filers). The reduction will be fully phased in by tax year 2027'.
new-york._programQuote: paidfamilyleave.ny.gov/2027: 'For 2027, employees will contribute 0.452% of their gross wages per pay period, with a maximum annual contribution of $451.81.'

colorado.label: Colorado's 2027 deduction, which is the federal standard deduction
colorado.what: Colorado starts from federal taxable income, so the 2027 federal standard deduction carries through to the state tax.
colorado._quote: Rev. Proc. 2026-35 section 3.15(1): 'For taxable years beginning in 2027, the standard deduction amounts under § 63(c)(2) are as follows:' with $33,200 joint, $24,925 head of household, $16,600 unmarried. The state link is tax.deductionFromFederal in tax-data-2026.json.

north-dakota.what: North Dakota starts from federal taxable income, so the 2027 federal standard deduction carries through to the state tax.
north-dakota._quote: Rev. Proc. 2026-35 section 3.15(1): 'For taxable years beginning in 2027, the standard deduction amounts under § 63(c)(2) are as follows:' with $33,200 joint, $24,925 head of household, $16,600 unmarried. The state link is tax.deductionFromFederal in tax-data-2026.json.

iowa._quote: Rev. Proc. 2026-35 section 3.15(1): 'For taxable years beginning in 2027, the standard deduction amounts under § 63(c)(2) are as follows:' with $33,200 joint, $24,925 head of household, $16,600 unmarried. The state link is tax.deductionFromFederal in tax-data-2026.json.

washington.label: Washington's 2027 paid leave premium
washington.what: Washington's paid leave premium goes up in 2027: 1.2% of pay, 70.7% of it paid by you, up to the 2027 Social Security limit.
washington._quote: paidleave.wa.gov/updates: 'The premium rate will be 1.2%.' 'Employers will pay 29.3% of the total premium and employees will pay 70.7%.' 'collect premiums up to the Social Security cap.' 0.012 x 0.707 = 0.008484; cap $192,300 from SSA's 2027 fact sheet.
